title: Email Service (Gmail)
summary: Design a large-scale email service: sending, receiving, storing, searching, and filtering spam.
statement: Design an email service like Gmail. It sends and receives mail over standard protocols, stores each user mailbox durably, supports search and labels, and filters spam and malware. Start by clarifying requirements and estimating scale, then design the system and defend your decisions.
initialGuidance: Clarify the users, the main journeys, and what is explicitly out of scope before drawing anything.
Estimate read and write volume and storage growth; the numbers decide which components you need.
Name the guarantees you will offer (consistency, durability, availability) and the trade-offs behind them.
Write down assumptions as you make them and revisit them when requirements change.
coreFunctionalRequirements: Store mailboxes with folders and labels.
Support attachments and sync across clients.

requirementQuestions.question: How many users and how much mail per day?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Sets read and write rates and storage growth, which decide whether a single node can cope.

requirementQuestions.question: Can a delivered email ever be lost?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Drives replication, backup, and write acknowledgement policy.

requirementQuestions.question: How quickly must inbound mail appear and search results return?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Defines which paths need caching, precomputation, or regional placement.

requirementQuestions.question: How is spam, phishing, and sender authenticity handled?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Introduces authentication, authorisation, and privacy constraints that affect the design.

requirementQuestions.question: Mailbox size limits and retention policies?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Determines the data model, retention, and storage choices.

requirementQuestions.question: Which protocols (SMTP, IMAP, web API) must be supported?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Fixes what is in and out of the design so effort goes to what matters.

workloadAssumptions.illustrativeNote: All numbers below are illustrative examples for practice and are not benchmarks. Real answers depend on the requirements the candidate negotiates.

estimationPrompts: How much storage do mailboxes need in total?
How many inbound messages per second reach the filters?
How large is the search index per user?

keyDecisions.question: How is incoming mail processed?
considerations: SMTP front ends accept and queue mail.
Authentication checks (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and spam filtering before delivery.

keyDecisions.question: How are mailboxes stored?
considerations: Partition by user so a mailbox lives on one shard with replicas.

keyDecisions.question: How is search provided?
considerations: Per-user inverted index updated on delivery.

keyDecisions.question: How is spam controlled?
considerations: Reputation, content models, and user feedback loops.

tradeoffs.tension: Blocking spam versus losing legitimate mail.
Search coverage versus storage and compute.

commonMistakes: Treating mail delivery as a single synchronous request.
One global index across all users.
No retry and queue strategy for temporary remote failures.
followUps: How do you provide conversation threading?
How do you handle a user with a 100 GB mailbox?
How do you migrate mailboxes between shards?
How do you support offline clients with IMAP?
